result.rationale: In AddGuestsDialog.tsx, isInvalidEmail is set true on validation failure and only reset in the cancel button's onClick; a successful submit path (handleAdd/addGuestsMutation.onSuccess) never resets it, so the error banner persists for the next session of the dialog. The client uniqueness check (Set equality on raw emails) and server-side filter also use different rules (server lowercases only for the blacklist comparison), confirming drift between the two hand-maintained validators. This is minor but a real, verifiable defect in the diff.

judged_text: The Zod email-uniqueness schema and the handler's duplicate filter are two parallel hand-maintained validations, and the dialog resets `isInvalidEmail` only in the cancel path, never when the user fixes the input. Once the user triggers the invalid-email banner, it stays rendered after they correct the emails and successfully submit, because `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on cancel; the server-side uniqueGuests check also uses different rules (case-sensitivity) than the client schema, so the two validators drift and produce different accept/reject answers for the same input.

Once the user triggers the invalid-email banner, it stays rendered after they correct the emails and successfully submit, because `isInvalidEmail` is only reset on cancel; the server-side uniqueGuests check also uses different rules (case-sensitivity) than the client schema, so the two validators drift and produce different accept/reject answers for the same input.

adjudication.rationale: The dialog’s invalid-email banner can persist incorrectly: `isInvalidEmail` is set to `true` on failed validation, but it is only reset in the Cancel button handler; it is not reset on successful submission (`onSuccess` only closes the dialog and resets `multiEmailValue`). Since the dialog component stays mounted under `BookingListItem`, reopening it after a prior invalid attempt can show the banner even when the inputs are reset. Also, client and server validations are indeed divergent: the client enforces uniqueness via `refine`, while the server schema (`addGuests.schema.ts`) only checks `.email()` and the handler’s `uniqueGuests` filtering does not dedupe duplicates within `guests` and compares emails case-sensitively against existing attendees/blacklist (blacklist is lowercased but `guest` is not), so the same input can be accepted/rejected differently.
